ai.description: *Cnemaspis ornata* reaches 45 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with a distinct yellow vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Key features include a slender body and prominent, keeled dorsal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis ornata* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange vertebral stripe that contrasts sharply against its dark, mottled body.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis ornata* inhabits rocky outcrops and boulders within moist deciduous forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 300 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Cnemaspis ornata* is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rocky surfaces and tree trunks within its habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis ornata* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity observed during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis ornata* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, India, typically inhabiting rocky areas at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
